newsitem.title: CANADA: Crystallex blames share drop on confusion.
newsitem.headline: Crystallex blames share drop on confusion.

text.p: Crystallex International Corp said on Wednesday that a 50 percent drop in its stock price today was due to investor confusion over a Venezeulan Supreme Court ruling in its dispute with Placer Dome Inc (PDG.TO over the Las Cristinas gold property.
Crystallex's stock sank 4.20 to close at 3.80 on volume of 3.4 million shares on the Toronto Stock Exchange on Wednesday.
"The general public is not aware of the Venezuelan system and so they get spooked and it's understandable," Crystallex Chief Executive Marc Oppenheimer said in a telephone interview.
Crystallex has argued that its unit, Inversora Mael, was the rightful owner of the property's 4 and 6 concessions.

Lawyers for Placer Dome argued that while the court recognized Crystallex's right to challenge the removal of copper rights at the concession, an earlier removal of gold exploration rights was ratified on Tuesday.
But Crystallex contends that if the court rules that Mael has valid title to the copper concessions, "by implication, it must also have determined that Mael owns the gold concessions."
Oppenheimer said he expected the company's lawyers would launch a court challenge regarding its copper rights next week.
He said the company was still willing to reach an out-of- court settlement with Placer Dome.
"We've always stated that we're flexible," he said.
